one_line: Shared-page conversion and consent layer for agent-callable WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: LeadMCP adds gates, human confirmation, attribution, citations, and consent-aware state to WebMCP tool calls.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: the product addresses the missing shared human/agent state after a tool call, including suspended confirmation and attribution that generic UI driving would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes human confirmation, cited results, consent-aware gates, and attribution as the product's purpose.
About text distinguishes LeadMCP from ordinary tool registration and describes a call that suspends on a person's decision.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent library plus a live production-site deployment, and frames a specific workflow, but the available frames do not clearly show an end-to-end gate/consent flow or tool trace.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo and public repository.
Frame sheet shows progression from a prompt screen to a populated workspace, but text and exact result are unclear.
impact_rationale: It targets a concrete problem for SaaS teams whose free tools are used by agents: lost funnel visibility and consent/attribution failures.
impact_evidence: About text identifies missing analytics events, bypassed email gates, and silent lead creation as the problem.
Pitch names trustworthy shared-page workflows and consent-aware gates.
creativity_rationale: The conversion/consent layer and human-decision-suspending tool call are a fresh extension of WebMCP beyond registration wrappers.
creativity_evidence: About text explicitly positions the project as the conversion half of WebMCP rather than another registration wrapper.
The shared-page gate and suspended human decision are distinctive interaction ideas.
usability_note: The intended workflow is understandable, but the frame evidence is too small to assess interaction polish.
red_flags: No transcript; frame text is largely illegible.
End-to-end consent and attribution behavior is claimed but not visibly verified in frames.
standouts: Human confirmation and consent-aware shared state are meaningful design choices.
advance_reason: High leverage and credible audience/problem fit; execution evidence is partial but sufficient for advancement.

one_line: An AI buyer negotiates with a store AI and receives a real Shopify discount code.
what_it_does: Haggle exposes product discovery, negotiation, offer, state, and deal-acceptance tools, then connects the accepted deal to normal checkout.
leverage_rationale: The negotiation protocol is a structured multi-round agent interaction with shared state and a real checkout consequence; generic UI automation would be markedly less reliable and less composable.
leverage_evidence: About text lists five negotiation tools and describes up to six server-side rounds.
Accepted deals mint a single-use product-scoped discount code and Shopify tools share the same document.modelContext surface.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is unusually complete from negotiation through discount-code issuance and checkout integration; frames visibly show the product and negotiation/deal concept, though not a full live checkout trace.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows Haggle landing page, negotiation chat, apparent deal result, and architecture flow.
About text claims a live Shopify catalog and real discount-code-to-checkout loop.
impact_rationale: Online shoppers and merchants have a clear mutual use case: agent-mediated negotiation while preserving merchant price floors and ordinary checkout.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies AI-assisted price negotiation ending in a real Shopify checkout.
About text explains the buyer/merchant incentive and product-scoped, time-limited discount.
creativity_rationale: AI-to-AI bargaining that resolves into a redeemable commerce artifact is a memorable and deeply pursued WebMCP interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Frame sheet shows buyer/store negotiation roles and a deal-result state.
Multi-round offers, server-side seller decisions, and a single-use code create a distinctive interaction.
usability_note: The negotiation-to-checkout story is clear and the human remains the final decision-maker; fine UI usability is only partly visible.
red_flags: Frames do not expose readable tool-call names or a complete checkout completion.
standouts: WebMCP is used for structured negotiation state rather than a superficial button wrapper.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity with a credible, visibly demonstrated commerce interaction.

one_line: A watchable, repeatable 3D rover benchmark for agent performance on a fixed track.
what_it_does: Torque Run lets agents drive a rover exclusively through WebMCP tools and compares runs by time, energy, integrity, and leaderboard identity.
leverage_rationale: The structured tool surface is the benchmark interface and enables identical seeded physics, inspectable calls, repeatability, and cross-agent comparison; screen-driving cannot provide the same reliability or comparability.
leverage_evidence: About text says all gameplay is exposed as WebMCP tools and tools are the only way to drive.
Fixed seeded track, persistent leaderboard, and vendor/model/prompt identity make runs repeatable and comparable.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and substantial, with a 3D arena, telemetry, hazards, scoring, and leaderboard; frames show setup and gameplay states but not a clearly readable completed run result.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows the 3D rover arena, benchmark branding, onboarding/read-before-intents modal, and gameplay UI.
About text specifies course hazards, battery constraint, scoring, call log, and leaderboard.
impact_rationale: It provides real value to developers and researchers who need an observable, repeatable way to compare agent strategies and harnesses.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies a common benchmark problem and a live identical track for agents.
About text describes model/prompt/harness comparison and inspectable spectator experience.
creativity_rationale: Turning WebMCP agent evaluation into watchable agentic esports with a physicalized rover challenge is a novel, memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Frame sheet shows MODEL vs MODEL/AGENT vs AGENT and WEBMCP, BUT WATCHABLE framing.
Optional cargo-cell objective, physics hazards, and spectator call log deepen the concept.
usability_note: The watchable race and explicit setup/read-before-intents flow are legible; detailed controls are too small to judge.
red_flags: Frames imply but do not clearly expose individual tool invocations or final score breakdown.
standouts: WebMCP is structurally indispensable to benchmark fairness.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and a highly original, credible benchmark/game format; visible product evidence supports advancement.
